utterances.text: But then how did you come to say, with no qualification at all, yes, Mr. Stanisic was involved with the discussions about the medals to the investigator three years ago?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible, I'm certain that I said that, but even then, I was thinking in those terms, namely that Stanisic had known about the entire activity, of course, it's not something insignificant, and he must have known about it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. And to keep Mr. Zecevic happy, you did, in fact, tell the investigator that, if we look at, please, page 165 in English and presumably the next page in B/C/S as well. Yes, we can see it at the top there, that Radovic was the trusted man of Mico Stanisic, went to Mico Stanisic in Belgrade to consult him and get the final decision. Now pausing there for a moment, the final decision had to be the minister's, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And I think he returned very quickly, maybe a day after tomorrow, the day after, and I know that the list which was verified again suffered certain changes, amendments, changes. Of course, part of us were unhappy with such corrections, or, however, I heard later that Radovic did not even see Stanisic and that he, on his own initiative, changed the proposal. What's true about those stories, I really don't know today. Right. Who told you that Mico Stanisic didn't know anything about the proposals that Radovic on his own had changed them?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not wish to change my statement given three years ago. My conviction and the information I have are such. I still today claim that based on the information I had, things transpired the way I said. Now, whether there were any changes under what circumstances I do not have any further information about that. There's nothing I can add to what I've said.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, you can. Who told you that Radovic never saw Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Someone must have, but at this moment, I cannot remember who. Must have been someone serious, someone who had such information in his hands because, otherwise, I wouldn't have believed the information.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you've told us yesterday that you saw Goran Macar quite recently. Was it him who told you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm -- I'm really sorry, Your Honours. I have to intervene in this -- in this situation. Ms. Korner just read to the witness his explanation, his answer, that he gave three years ago and in that particular place, he mentions the very same issue, that he heard that Nenad Radovic did not ever went to see Mico Stanisic. Now, implying that he saw somebody in between before his testimony over here clearly is without any merit.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. And I didn't mean -- when I said, saw him yesterday, it's my fault, I accept that. It was a bad question.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Was it Goran Macar who told you this?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot remember. There is no reason why I wouldn't remember. It is possible, but I cannot tell you now, cannot remember it now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: You live in Bijeljina, don't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... as does Macar?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. As well as Dobro Planojevic and many other people I co-operated in 1992 and later.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... Stanisic's brother-in-law live there?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to my information, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... is he somebody that you know?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know of him. I know that he's Mico Stanisic son -- brother-in-law, but I wouldn't even recognise him. I don't know what he looks like.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: So you have never had any meetings with him or discussed any of this with him?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's just, finally, on this topic, just look at the some of the people who were awarded medals. Did you see the list before it went off?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can you have a look, please, in that --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, sorry. Have I asked for the list to be put up? No. Document 1281 -- oh, sorry, P732.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, are aware that you are nearly 60 minutes over the three hours that you requested?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, but you don't surprise me, Your Honour. But it has taken some time. If Your Honours don't want me to go through this, I won't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: The -- the -- we -- of course, take -- expect that counsel know where they are going, but we are at a loss as to where this line of questions that has engaged the past 30 minutes or so has been taking us in terms of relevance. We don't immediately appreciate the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, if -- in that case, Your Honours, perhaps I can -- I thought we had looked at this document before but maybe we haven't. Can we just look at some of the people who were given some serious gongs, if I can put it that way. Can we have the third page, second page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: These were medals were awarded in 1993, it would appear; is that right, Mr. Njegus?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. Second page in English, and still the first page, I think, in B/C/S -- yes, B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Karadjordjevo Star, the first class commendation, is that a seriously impressive medal?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Number 5, Simo Drljaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, as we can see.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... 1993, were people aware of what had happened in Omarska and Keraterm in the camps that were run by the Prijedor police?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure if you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I am asking you. Didn't anybody, when you had discussions about giving Mr. Drljaca this medal, say, Would that be the right thing to do, given he was in charge of the Prijedor camps?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see where you're going, and if you want me to comment this, I can, in a few sentences, explain things further. The initiative came from Tomo Kovac, and according to my views, at the time, maybe, but certainly now, this whole thing was done with too much haste. It was only several months after the events and the process was initiated, I don't know to what degree, Mr. Stanisic was familiar with it. I told you about the two versions. And it is true, as you say, that we can find here a few names who are on the list who did receive commendations, very high rank. But that's a fact. What can one do it about it? This is my comment.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Well, I don't think I'll go through any of the other names.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I appreciate that I'm well over the time, and I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If you will just bear with me, Your Honours, one moment, while I organise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good day, Mr. Njegus. My name is Slobodan Zecevic. We haven't had an opportunity to meet before. You refused to have any conversations with the Defence.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I thought I should introduce myself. Sir, I'll start with the last questions put by Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, when Ms. Korner asked for a document, which is this witness's statement made in 2007, we haven't heard the number, I don't know how to ask for this document to be put up, but I believe that Registrar can assist us. I will be needing page 146 and 147 in the Serbian version, and I assume 164 and 165 in the English version. I am being told it is 65 ter 9035. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the interview, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course, I do remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I need page 146 in the Serbian version, which is 164 in the English version. And then, later on, 147, and 165 respectively. As can you see here, sir, you were asked about the commendation or medal that you received as well, and the Prosecutor asked you the year is important was it 1992 or 1993. You said that. And you respond, I don't remember when the decision was reached and then you say, I really cannot remember if it was in 1992. It must have been late 1992. And also it is possible that it was at the very beginning of 1993.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you confirm that here, that the medals may have been awarded in 1993; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Further in the text, we can find the same lines that were read by Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we now please have page 147 in Serbian version and 165 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here you can see in the first paragraph we can see your answer. This is what you are saying. It's somewhere in the middle of this text. We have most probably verified the proposal but there were certain changes to it. After that, Nenad Radovic, who was at the time -- I don't know what he was at the time but I think was at the position of chief of cabinet, he was the trusted man of Mico Stanisic. I know that he took that verified proposal and went to Mico Stanisic in Belgrade to consult him and get the final decision. I think he returned rather quickly, maybe tomorrow or the day after. And I know that the lists which was verified suffered certain amendments changes. Of course, parts of us were unhappy with such corrections, however, I heard later that Nenad Radovic did not even see Mico Stanisic and that he put in the changes to the proposal on his own initiative. What's true about this story, I really don't know. So this is what you said in 2007, and when answering to Ms. Korner you gave the exact -- exactly the same answer. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Njegus, let us take a look at the document P732. You will remember, Mr. Njegus, that the government -- that the government, where Mr. Mico Stanisic was the minister of the interior, after the 24th of November, 1992, when the prime minister returned his mandate to the Assembly was disbanded. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember the events, but I cannot tell you when exactly did that take place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, is it not, that since the government stopped functioning, together with the prime minister, all the ministers had to return their mandates and as of that moment Mico Stanisic, as the minister of the interior, carried out only technical part of the work.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's something that is described as -- as a care-taker government.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, please take a look at this document -- take a good look at it. In the preamble and when one is reading documents, it is very important to read that introductory piece. Here we can see that they quote the regulations according to which the president of the Republic, Radovan Karadzic, issued a decree on awarding medals. Among other items mentioned, there is the Law on Commendations and Recognitions, the "Official Gazette" of the Republika Srpska number 4, year 1993. I will put it to you that this Law on Commendations and Recognitions of Republika Srpska and this "Official Gazette" 4/1993 was published on the 8th of April, 1993. In other words, the commendations were only distributed after that date. That's obvious.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're asking me, I would say anything is possible. It is possible that this all may have happened during the second mandate of Mr. Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is what we're trying to determine here, because here you stated that this is something from 1992 or 1993, and I'm stating here that in the introductory part one is quoting a law that was enacted on the 28th of April 1993, which means that the events took place after the law was enacted.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That shows that obviously that all the activities took place during the second mandate when Mr. Stanisic was appointed minister for the second time.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Since the situation is not relevant for these proceedings, we will drop the subject. Thank you, Mr. Njegus.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, it's a convenient point to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a convenient point now. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just a few more questions in relation to the previous issue. I did say that we'd finished it, but there are a few more things that I wanted to clear up. Sir, it's a fact, isn't it, that Mr. Mico Stanisic was the minister of the interior for the second time between April of 1993 until April of 1994.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter is not sure whether he has given the right date for the beginning of the second mandate.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To clarify, I'll say this slowly. Mico Stanisic, his second mandate, was from January 1994 until April 1994. I'm not saying this because of you, sir, because the interpreters didn't hear me right and mistranslated it. And your response to this question was, because we don't have your answer in the transcript either.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are most probably right, because you're better at determining when happened -- when what happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, I put to you that these medals were issued on the 21st of November, on the St. Archangel Day, so all of these medals that were awarded by the President of the Republic were distributed on the 21st of November, 1993, on Jahorina mountain, on archangel's day and that there Tomo Kovac was the one who gave them the medals?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you're right. Now I'm beginning to remember the events, because I remember it was the -- the snow was deep. It was winter-time. I was travelling with a colleague of mine from Bijeljina. I know his name. We had problems with the car, and we managed to get there in time for the awards ceremony, but I think it took place on Pale at Koran, Pale facility. Yes, you're right, you refreshed my memory.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I would like to have P1434 put up on the screen. It is a document that the Prosecutor showed to you just a moment ago, and we need to go back to it and look at the document again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 218. Admitted perhaps two hours ago, as P1434 [sic].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 1434.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit P1423 for the counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm really sorry. I copied it from the transcript. Perhaps there was a mistake. Could we zoom in for the witness on the signature, that you looked at with the Prosecutor, the signature and the stamp. Sir, you remember discussing it with the Prosecutor. The Prosecutor asked you how you explained that Mr. Mico Stanisic signed this. You said it was not your job to go into that, and you gave some other explanations. I put it to you that before the typewritten words "minister of the interior" there are words, letters POM, probably meaning assistant, and the signature is that of Mico Vujicic not Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is indubitable. When you zoom in on it and look at it carefully I can confirm what the counsel just said. It says POM, meaning assistant minister, and it is Petar Vujicic in the signature, and I knew Petar Vujicic. There was this similar document that order from Karadzic we looked at yesterday where I thought I recognised the handwriting of Petar Vujicic, but that wasn't really right. This one is, the signature of Petar Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To be completely clear, can we show the witness P876. This is good. Now, the fifth column from the left, just below the picture of Mr. Stanisic, needs to be enlarged, if possible. This is good. Perfect.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is in English. I will read it out to you. It says: "05, administration for analytics and information, and it says: Assistant minister for the administration, for statistics and information Petar Vujicic." Is that the person we were talking about?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It seems then quite logical that assistant minister, Petar Vujicic writes to you as another assistant minister in charge of a different area, requesting a draft rule-book for disciplinary measures to be presented.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether he did on his own initiative or he was moved by someone else, but, in any case he did that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We see here that you were head of administration 04.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think we made that quite clear. I was acting in that position without formal appointment.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now see P1422.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to shed more light on these documents that have been shown to you earlier today while they're still fresh in everyone's mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] P1422.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this document dated 15 June? You discussed it with the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I objected during that examination, claiming that it was not an order to mobilize but, that, instead, this order gives an assignment to a certain unit, to round up conscripts who had failed to refuse -- who had failed to respond to the call-up issued by authority of the Presidency of the Republic of the 20th of May. And that means that you will agree with me, that the Presidency of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina made the decision on mobilisation. Isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I agreed with that earlier on. And I agree with it again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, in paragraph 2 it says that the conscripts mentioned in paragraph 1 should be turned over to the Lukavica Barracks. Isn't that a military barracks?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So this unit of the Ministry of the Interior, after rounding up these persons who had failed to respond to mobilisation voluntarily, should hand over these people to the military authorities?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the gist of this order. Now how and why it was issued is something we discussed earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let's look at another document you've already seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's P1420.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You remember this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Although I didn't read every word, but I remember, in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we turn to page 2 in both versions. And now could we zoom in on the third paragraph where we see the number 18/92. It's the first paragraph on the English page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you read this out for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will. It says: In view of -- in view of everything indicated above, and referencing our document number such and such, dated 20th April, 1992, and I repeat that the heads of Security Services Centre are obliged to obtain the approval of the minister of the interior for the assignment of employees to certain positions (head of the National Security Service sector, head of the public Security Service Centre, head of public security station, commander of the police station, commander of police station departments, and chief of the crime department). Therefore, with regard to these employees, approach the ministry, and concerning other employees make staffing decisions on your own.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what's written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: That means, Mr. Njegus, that the key positions in CSBs - and when I say "key positions," that means chiefs of sectors of national and public security, station commanders, chiefs of public security stations and the chief of the criminal investigation department - could not, as a rule, and by the rules, and in keeping with this document, be appointed without prior approval of the minister and the ministry.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I agree with everything you said.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now if you can look at the last paragraph in the document, you discussed these stamps with my learned friend yesterday. Now, the last paragraph before the signature says: "This ministry has taken certain measures to develop new seals of the Ministry of the Interior, the CSB, and the SJB. And until they are finalized, please use the existing seals."

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We'll go back to -- we'll come back to stamps a bit earlier -- a bit later, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show the witness 1D73.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, the previous document we discussed was dated 26 April. And this document is dated 25 April, the day before, giving authority to chiefs of CSBs. And the paragraph 2 specifies which officials, which appointments, and which kind of duties need prior approval of the minister, for someone to be assigned to them. This is related to the document we've just discussed.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's obvious.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now show the witness P1421.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, you've also seen this document earlier today, describing the status of personnel in the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina dated June 1992, 8th June 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And just to make your answer more complete, I would like to ask you to look at paragraph 2, which says: No information is available as to how many employees there are in individual CSBs or public security stations and no information is available on the number of employees who transferred from the former MUP and how many are newly hired, and there is no information about how many staff are engaged in specific areas of work or the number of retired MUP employees. The fact is the information you had was very limited, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. You are right. Now, if you look at this report more carefully you will see my handwriting in the top right corner which says, Pero for the progress report, which means that the work I did with a couple of my assistants was an attachment, a contribution, to Petar Vujicic who was in charge of analytics and information, so that he can make his progress report as complete as possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: At that time, you did not have information from the CSB Banja Luka, because it was early June, and the fact is that the corridor was established only in July, or perhaps even later, in 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On page 2 of this document --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we show page 2 to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In the third paragraph, you include the reservation about the reliability of this information because you say, the information available to the personnel service is not completely reliable because the information we receive is not up to date. And then you criticise some other services. And you say, in some cases two appointments were issued from the -- for the same job. In other cases, there are people who don't have a formal appointment, yet other staff is actually engaged in a completely different kind of work than in their job description. You also note that in some cases, employment contracts were issued even to reserve police officers. Now, if I understand this correctly, and I'd like you to confirm, it means that the reliability of this information is very relative, because you say that the amount of information you have is limited and even the information you have is rather unreliable and not up to date.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. This is a very problematic report. It was made just a few months into the war. What else could we do, if we were doing this work alone, just me and perhaps one or two assistants? We had no information about reservists and about many other things. My duty, when I took up this job, was to try to improve -- to improve the quality of information we were receiving and we were able to pass on, and certainly what you noted at the beginning is perfectly correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: On the previous page in this document, you are making proposals for measures to be taken.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That is on page 3. Page 3 of the Serbian version, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You can see the proposals for measures. And the item numbers are from 1 to 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If we could see them because I want to comment on only one of these items. It will -- which is on the following page in both language versions, page 5 in English and page 4 in Serbian and I mean item 8.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Here, too, you say: "Immediately cease issuing standard decisions bearing the minister's signature. Decisions without the approval of the responsible superior and in case of supervisory positions, decisions without the approval of the responsible managers and the minister." If we put that into the context of what we have discussed, you are indicating that you have information about some instances where standard decisions are issued with the -- with the facsimile of the minister's signature or without the knowledge of the supervisors in the CSBs and SJBs. Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you are here making a proposal that this practice stop immediately, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please show the witness 1D03-1232.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Let me just -- let us just briefly comment on one of your letters from November 1992. I suppose, actually, it's yours. You will tell us. It's about the stamps I had said that we would comment on.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please blow this up for Mr. Njegus to be able to see.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This document was drafted in Bijeljina, as you see, in November 1992. At that point in time your administration was in Bijeljina, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It says assistant minister and your name. I don't know if it is your signature.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And you say here that you have information that there are some stamp makers who make stamps that are not authorised by the MUP which was actually a legal requirement; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is a fact, sir, isn't it, that in the former SFRY, and the practice has continued, I believe, to the present day, that all stamp makers must have an authorisation issued by the MUP to do that job; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And you can see that here, too, I made an effort to introduce order in these activities. Obviously Minister Stanisic didn't value these efforts highly, but that's another story.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: But, certainly, Minister Stanisic, too, if I've correctly understood your testimony so far, also insisted on introducing the rule of law; that is, the respect for laws and regulations; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is not at issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let us move onto a different topic, sir. Yesterday, and to a smaller extent today also, you spoke to my learned friend -- oh, I apologise, I'm being reminded.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So yesterday, while giving evidence, and also at the beginning of your testimony today, mention was made of the order dated 15 May about the organisation of the MUP, in accordance with the decree on the declaration of imminent threat of war. Do you remember saying that?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Njegus, in the SFRY, a federal law on All People's Defence and social self-protection was in force. And there were also laws at republican levels about All People's Defence and social self-protection, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my period, the time of the League of Communists. I know that very well, yes, with all the directives concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that, under that law any institution, including the MUP, was duty-bound to draft war plans and have a wartime structure in case of war or imminent threat of war; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's a fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's also a fact, isn't it, that in accordance with the former -- or structure, that is, in the Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia and all the socialist republics, including Bosnia-Herzegovina, it was mandatory for every SJB to have a -- an officer in charge of drafting a wartime structure of the MUP and war plans; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: After the establishment of the RS, I suppose you know that all laws and regulations of the former SFRY, as well as the laws and regulations of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, were being applied in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That is, all rules and regulations that were not contrary to the interest of the Serbian people, I believe was the language. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We understand each other. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You agreed with me, so it's a fact that the Law on All People's Defence and social self-protection, either the federal law or the law of Bosnia and Herzegovina was also implemented in the territory of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina in 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in force, if that's what you mean. Whether it was really implemented is another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that the duty to prepare a wartime structure which included certain procedures and a job classification was adopted at the level of the MUP of the Republic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: We're referring to the time when the SFRY existed; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This order of 15 May, which is 1D46, an exhibit shown to you yesterday, of which you said that it was not implemented in practice, was the result of the requirements that existed under the law at that moment. Will you agree with me?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, well, formally speaking you're certainly right. But as far as I'm concerned and the content of this document, this order, and that it really was implemented is not an open issue to me. Because the war had started. How can you organise anything in wartime if you have a peacetime structure? That would be impossible. Even if we disregard the formal aspect of it. That would be my answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: You certainly remember, and I can show you the document too, that the rules on the internal organisation of the MUP under conditions of imminent threat of war and in wartime, was only adopted at sometime in 1993. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that in the early days, after the establishment of the MUP, we didn't have that.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see 65 ter 2749. That is an excerpt from the rules on internal organisation which contains some schematics.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember this document, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: So I don't want to go into the details of the document because it isn't especially interesting us to as we're dealing with 1992. But I would like to establish a link between these two documents, the one dated 15 May and this one from 1993. That is, only in 1993, when the rules on the internal organisation were adopted, it replaced -- or they replaced the order dated 15 May and outlines the real structure and the way of functioning of the MUP under conditions of imminent threat of war or wartime conditions. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes and no. This document is what it is, and it was really adopted only in early 1993. But I don't see how it could replace that order about the establishment of that staff because it was never implemented, so ... this would be my comment to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What I wanted to say but maybe wasn't able to express myself very clearly, was that the order dated 15 May could not be implemented because at the time there were no rules on the internal structure. That was part of my suggestion.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, among others.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there is opposition, and I suppose there isn't, because it's a 65 ter document of the Prosecution, 2749, I seek to tender it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D318, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Hvala.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Njegus, yesterday during the examination-in-chief you may not remember, but I'll try to remind you without reading the pages to you. You spoke about the MUP really being created from scratch. I believe that's -- those are roughly the words that you used. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, exactly. That's how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, isn't it, that the MUP, and you spoke about your administration being a very important administration in any Ministry of the Interior, and therefore also for the MUP of the RS, that you and your administration were, at first, alone, then you had an assistant; and then, throughout 1992, I believe you only had five to six staff. Correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, these are facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Even though there was such a small number of you, your administration drafted a huge number of instructions and other documents; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we made -- did our utmost under the given conditions.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It's a fact, sir, isn't it, that the entire MUP in the headquarters in the first few months, up until the summer of 1992, hardly had 40 staff, including the minister and all assistants.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps even fewer than that; whereas, the former MUP of the BiH may have had as many as 400 staff in headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: When I say "40 staff," I include drivers, technical staff, secretaries, et cetera, right?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: To give an illustration of the work of your administration, I would like to show document 1D00-2996. Do you remember this letter of yours which was sent to the under-secretary and the administrations of the MUP where you put forward an initiative to receive possible amendments to the Law on The MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it bears my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: It is dated 23 September 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there is opposition, I seek to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D319, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I don't know whether it's necessary to point out to you or maybe just to read out to you some of the instructions that I assume were drafted by your administration. For instance, administration of urgent, current occasional reporting in the organs of the interiors.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the context. You need not read it.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The reference is 1D51.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Sir, let me ask you about some other instructions. The biggest parts of work was to draft the rules that was -- that were drafted during 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: And the rules, it was necessary to get proposals from the various stations and centres from the ground, and this was going on throughout 1992.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. The lawyers who never worked on a document such as that one cannot understand how huge and comprehensive this task is.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For your reference, this document bears the number P615. Here, among other documents, we have P850. This is the Rules on Internal Organisation of the Republican Secretariat of Internal Affairs of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. The rules of Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were applied for all practical purposes in the Ministry of the Interior of Republika Srpska throughout 1992 until the moment the rules that you worked on was adopted in 1993.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly so.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember the instruction concerning modes of behaviour and internal relationships between officers of the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the so-called green book.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: For your reference, it's D -- P150, from September 1992. Do I need to show you this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, there's no need. This document is a constitution for every police officer.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: A moment ago we discussed a letter of yours -- letter you've recognised the signature of Mr. Vujicic, for which you had thought earlier it was the signature of Mr. Stanisic, and then you changed your position. Mr. Vujicic proposed for -- a proposal to be made regarding the rules regarding disciplinary responsibility of the workers of the Ministry of the Interior under war conditions. We have document D54 here. This document represents the rule-book in question, which was forwarded on the 19th of September 1992. Do you remember the document, or do I need to show it to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no need. I know of this document as well. And I know that in accordance to this document, the authority for initiating and conducting disciplinary proceedings against members of the interior of Republika Srpska was transferred to the person we mentioned, the chiefs of centres, commander of the special unit, and maybe some others, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The essence of the rule-book is that, according to the rules, the disciplinary system, or the system of disciplinary responsibility, became more efficient, and the procedure was condensed.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that was the purpose. We wanted to use the rules to simplify the procedure concerning the conditions under which we operated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Of course the idea behind it was primarily to speed up and facilitate issuing of disciplinary measures against MUP members who violated their duties.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Another important element related to this rule-book, or rules is the fact that -- that the statute of limitation was extended, meaning that disciplinary procedures could be conducted in relation to events that may have taken earlier so that statute of limitations wouldn't put some incidents beyond the scope of disciplinary measures.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I can show you Article 17, if you want. If you remember that this article was in the rules, then there's no need.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember. You're most probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: The purpose of extending the statute of limitations was to make sure that all disciplinary violations would not remain unpunished.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the purpose of putting in such a provision was exactly that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember, sir, that rules on the form of the ID documents by the official workers of the Ministry of Interior was adopted in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have 1D00-0644 on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This is a cover letter from the 19th of September.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please have the rules, which is page 3 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: As I was saying, this is the cover letter that went with the document, and then now we see the rules. Do you remember the rules?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But of course. The activity that followed up, I was involved in that, not only myself, of course, 24 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: What activities did you mean?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What follows from the rules. Namely, the making of these IDs.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: There were cases when people were issued official IDs without foundation.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, no. In essence, all the police officers in former Bosnia and Herzegovina had just like in any other police force, their own IDs and later on police badge. With the start of the war, logically, new members joined the MUP of Republika Srpska, among other things. And in the meantime, there were some serious cases of abuse of such documents, both by staff members and other people, and those were the motives and reasons why relatively early we launched into this activity, and I think we managed to complete the task within a reasonable time-frame. We did a lot. We created a new ID format. And prior to that, we did some checkups on all of our staff members, got some documentation about them, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: In other words, this procedure was used for the purpose of --

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Introducing order, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unless there are objections, I seek to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, can I just, for a moment, ask where this document comes from and what the date is because it is not very clear on our screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is document of 19 September 1992. It comes from -- just a moment. From MUP of Republika Srpska. These are the rules, and it was confirmed by the witness that was adopted in 1992 and was applied for a certain period of time. I don't know exactly until when.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] I'm sorry. I have some reservations which I -- for reasons I won't trouble the Court with at the moment. Does the witness say that he recognises this document? Because he says, do you remember the document or do I need to show you? There's no need. I know this document -- I know of this document. Is he saying that he recognises it? That's all I want to know.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honours, I'm trying to save -- I'm really trying to save time because I want to rely on the existence of this document and actually the consequences of what this document meant for the establishment of Republika Srpska or introducing law and order within the MUP of Republika Srpska in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: We have a -- an ancillary question to the point Ms. Korner has raised and that is, what is the nature of these rules, whether they are purely internal departmental guide-lines or whether they fall into the category of -- of subsidiary legislation which should be part of the law library that we're building.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, let me try to explain. Your Honours, this is an part of the subsidiary.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honours. If this is going to affect the admission of this document then the witness ought not to be listening to this, and I believe the witness speaks English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Well, inasmuch as this appears to be a matter of some importance, let's marked for identification and move on. Because it may very well be that, upon the queries that Ms. Korner has raised being looked into, that we -- that this falls within and just is subsumed within the law library. But that remains to be seen.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I may be heard. With all due respect, I respectively disagree. First of all, the witness confirmed that he actually is the author of this -- of this -- of this -- of this rule-book. He is the author. It is -- it was under his auspices that this rule-book was created.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HARHOFF
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, I don't think that there is any major disagreement about allowing this document to come into evidence. The only question that remains is whether we give it a separate exhibit number now or whether we include in the law library.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I wanted to explain but Ms. Korner stood up and said that maybe the witness should be excused. I don't have anything against that. The witness can be excused, it will take me two minutes, and I will explain the nature of this document and all these rule-books and instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic, you just said something, which I confess I missed and Judge Delvoie as well, I don't know about Judge Harhoff. You said that the witness testified that he was part of the authorship of this?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] ... no.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Well, maybe it wasn't recorded. But we can ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE DELVOIE
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: May I ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the rules concerning the format of the ID of the official organs of the Ministry of Interior, was this document drafted by your administration, the administration you were at the head of in MUP?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not only our administration. Some other administrations also were involved. We were at the time in Bijeljina, and yes, this is what we drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Would you want me to show you this document in hard copy so that can you verify whether this is the document we are talking about? There's no need for us to go through every page.

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if necessary, I know what this document is all about.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Having regard to what I now understand the answer to be, the document be admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I want a simple, straightforward question (sic) before I withdraw my objection. I would like the witness to look at the document and confirm that he has seen this document before. And the reason is the provenance of the document. And to read the date, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know what this is all about. As I've told you, this was drafted in Bijeljina with the participation of two or three administrations including the analysis. I remember that they typed this in on their computer.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know the witness has difficulties. Perhaps he would like to answer the direct question that I asked, or -- I don't want to intervene, but Mr. Zecevic, can you ask the question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, the question is as follows: Have you seen this document before, and could you please read the date on the document. That was the question that Ms. Korner wanted to put. So we have the first two pages being the cover letter, and then we have the document itself, which is page 3. I would like to ask you to look at it again, because Ms. Korner insists. Have you seen the document before; and please read the date?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be perfectly honest, here on the cover letter, we see the date, 19 September 1992. I don't remember what was written in the cover letter. But as far as this rule-book is concerned, I remember we wrote it in Bijeljina. Two or three administrations were involved, and mine to a lesser extent. That's why I mentioned a moment ago the administration for analysis, which actually typed the text. And then we endorsed this document, and we applied it in practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Just reply very simply: Have you seen this document before, and if you have, can you confirm the date, August 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen this rule-book. Whether it was August or some other time, I can't say with any certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any reason to doubt what is written on the document? August 1992. Do you have reason to suspect that it was maybe written in September 1993?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: None whatsoever.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that in the second half of 1992 such a rule-book was in use in the MUP of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: RADOMIR NJEGUS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... explore this and I offer this into evidence if there is no objection from Ms. Korner again.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Thank you. I don't think he has answered the question, but I think this is n sufficient -- I withdraw my objection, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: As we said, the document is admitted and marked.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit 1D320, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
utterances.text: Which conveniently brings us to the time that we should rise for the day. There is two minutes left, but I don't know that you could usefully make use of that so we're back in this courtroom tomorrow morning at 9.00. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE HALL
